sentiment.rationale: The document reports a strong operational turnaround with record backlog ($682B), improved deliveries (600 commercial airplanes, highest since 2018), and positive free cash flow in Q4. Forward guidance is raised: management explicitly guides to positive free cash flow of $1B-$3B for 2026, up from a -$1.9B usage in 2025, and reiterates a path to $10B normalized free cash flow. While risks remain (KC-46A charge, 777X engine issue), the overall forward trajectory is clearly positive and management expresses confidence, warranting a moderately bullish score.

summary.revenue: Q4 2025 revenue of $23.9 billion, up 57% from $15.2 billion in Q4 2024. Full year 2025 revenue of $89.5 billion, up 34% from $66.5 billion in 2024.
summary.eps: Q4 2025 GAAP diluted EPS of $10.23, up from ($5.46) in Q4 2024. Core EPS (non-GAAP) of $9.92, up from ($5.90). Full year 2025 GAAP diluted EPS of $2.48, up from ($18.36). Core EPS of $1.19, up from ($20.38).
summary.guidance: Management expects 2026 free cash flow of $1B to $3B, positive for the full year. BCA deliveries expected up ~10% year-over-year. 737 deliveries expected around 500 aircraft, 787 deliveries expected 90-100. Management reiterated a path to $10B normalized free cash flow.
summary.margin: Q4 2025 GAAP operating margin of 36.7%, up from (24.7%) in Q4 2024. Core operating margin (non-GAAP) of 35.6%, up from (26.5%). Full year 2025 GAAP operating margin of 4.8%, up from (16.1%). Core operating margin of 3.6%, up from (17.8%).
key_risks: KC-46A program charge of $565 million driven by higher production support and supply chain costs.
Potential durability issue identified on 777X engine, working with GE to understand root cause and corrective action.
Delayed certification and first delivery on 777X program (first delivery still anticipated in 2027).
Customer considerations and excess advances related to prior delivery delays on 737 and 787 programs impacting cash flow.
DOJ payment expected in 2026, sliding from 2025.
Tariff and trade barrier risks, particularly with China and Europe.
Spirit AeroSystems integration and performance risks.
key_opportunities: Record backlog of $682 billion, including over 6,100 commercial airplanes.
Production rate increases planned: 737 to 47 per month later in 2026, 787 to 10 per month later in 2026.
777X program: strong demand, 202 orders in 2025, first delivery anticipated in 2027.
Defense, Space & Security: record backlog of $85 billion, transformational win for U.S. Air Force sixth-generation fighter (F-47).
Global Services: record annual orders of $28 billion, record backlog of $30 billion, double-digit margins.
Spirit AeroSystems acquisition expected to improve safety, quality, and production stability.
Path to $10 billion normalized free cash flow.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Management uses language like 'We made significant progress on our recovery in 2025 and have set the foundation to keep our momentum going' and 'I remain confident in our team and our plan to deliver on the opportunities and address the challenges in front of us in the year ahead.'

review_flags.reason: The score of 0.30 is based on forward guidance being raised (positive free cash flow in 2026 vs. negative in 2025) and confident management tone, but the document also contains significant risk disclosures (KC-46A charge, 777X engine issue, DOJ payment). A reviewer may want to assess whether the positive forward signal outweighs these risks sufficiently for a BUY signal.
